scriptText: Speaker: In the Arctic tundra, permafrost is a soil layer that has remained frozen for thousands of years. As global temperatures rise, permafrost thaws and dormant microbes become active. These microbes decompose organic material and release greenhouse gases such as carbon dioxide and methane. Permafrost stores roughly twice as much carbon as the atmosphere, so researchers use sophisticated models and data about microbial species to understand the feedback loops and the possible rise in atmospheric greenhouse gases.
